corrections.why: NYS Parks says the Coast Guard decommissioned the lighthouse in 1958; LF and Rowlett say the crew left and the light moved to the skeletal tower in 1958. USLHS gives 1959-1998 as the span of discontinuance, so the record's 1959 is one of several dates.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett lists 1998 as both a first-lit date and an inactive date for the two towers. Read together with LF, 1998 is when the beacon returned to the historic tower; the skeletal tower has been inactive since. The historic tower is the active light.
Construction began 28 April 1875 and the tower and dwelling were finished in January 1876 (LF). The lens was first shown 27 April 1876. Rowlett's 1875 date is the start of construction.

notes_for_editor: Facts from LighthouseFriends (LF) are used for the 1872-1876 construction, the keepers' personal details, the 1934 fog-signal contract, the 1958 removal and the 1998 relighting. The Light-House Board volumes for 1873-1890 are not in the local corpus, so the 1873 and 1875 appropriations and the 1877-1880 erosion facts rest on LF alone. Scan pages were checked against the corpus page index: the Board's 1891 and 1892 reports (186, 523), the Commissioner's 1921 estimates (690, printed 85), the 1935 Bulletin (p. 29) and the Life-Saving table of 1900 (406). The archive's keeper roster (NARA registers via USLHS, 33 lines) matches the keepers list line for line, with person slugs from roster.py --json; no keeper name was confirmed in a primary record this round. Disagreements left open: tower height (USLHS 53.5 ft / 16.3 m; LF seventy feet; Rowlett 61 ft / 18.5 m); focal height 71.5 ft (21.8 m) per USLHS; the years the light was out (NYS Parks and LF 1958; USLHS 1959-1998; Rowlett inactive 1958-1998); the Ontario's type (LF schooner; the 2008 account a sloop of war) and place (LF places her off this point; the 2008 account does not). The Life-Saving table's counts for Thirty-Mile Point are not legible in the scanned OCR, so no counts are used. The lens's whereabouts are unknown. The NRHP nomination (84003922) is not digitised at NPGallery; only the asset page (listing date, multiple listing) is used. A New-York Tribune page of 20 May 1894 (p. 17) matched only loosely (the keeper hit was housekeeper) and is not used.
